_how_to_edit: One question per {...}. 'question': the text. 'answers': exactly 4. 'correct': the position of the right answer (0 = first, 1 = second, 2 = third, 3 = fourth). Optional 'explanation' (shown after answering) and 'image' (an https:// link, or a file name inside the images/ folder). Answers are shuffled when shown. The bot re-reads this file automatically. After editing, run: python check_trivia.py

questions.question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury orbits closest to the Sun, completing a lap in just 88 Earth days.

questions.question: What is the largest planet in our Solar System?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is so big that all the other planets could fit inside it.

questions.question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars looks red because its surface is covered in rusty iron oxide dust.

questions.question: Which planet is famous for its bright, wide rings made of ice and rock?
questions.explanation: All four giant planets have rings, but Saturn's are by far the brightest and easiest to see.

questions.question: How many planets are in our Solar System?
questions.explanation: There are eight planets; Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

questions.question: What kind of object is the Sun?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a star, a huge ball of hot gas powered by nuclear fusion.

questions.question: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon on 20 July 1969 during Apollo 11.

questions.question: Who was the first human to travel into space?
questions.explanation: Yuri Gagarin orbited Earth aboard Vostok 1 on 12 April 1961.

questions.question: About how long does it take Earth to travel once around the Sun?
questions.explanation: One trip around the Sun takes about 365 and a quarter days, which is why we have leap years.

questions.question: What causes day and night on Earth?
questions.explanation: Earth spins once about every 24 hours, so each side takes turns facing the Sun.

questions.question: What mainly causes Earth's seasons?
questions.explanation: Earth's tilt means each hemisphere gets more direct sunlight at different times of year.

questions.question: Which planet is the hottest in our Solar System?
questions.explanation: Venus is hotter than Mercury because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat.

questions.question: What is the name of the galaxy we live in?
questions.explanation: Our Solar System is one of billions of star systems in the Milky Way.

questions.question: About how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.explanation: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to travel to Earth.

questions.question: What is a "shooting star" really?
answers: A meteor burning up in the atmosphere
questions.explanation: Shooting stars are small bits of space rock that glow as they burn up high in the sky.

questions.question: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a star, and it is much closer than any other!

questions.question: Can sound travel through the empty vacuum of space?
answers: No, sound needs something like air to travel through
Yes, even faster than on Earth
questions.explanation: Sound is a vibration of matter, so in empty space there is nothing to carry it.

questions.question: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.explanation: Your skin covers your whole body and protects everything inside.

questions.question: How many bones does a typical adult human have?
questions.explanation: Babies are born with around 300 bones, and many fuse together as they grow.

questions.question: Which organ pumps blood around your body?
questions.explanation: Your heart beats about 100,000 times a day.

questions.question: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explanation: The heart has two atria on top and two ventricles below.

questions.question: What is the smallest bone in the human body?
questions.explanation: The stapes, or stirrup bone, is only about 3 mm long.

questions.question: What is the longest bone in the human body?
questions.explanation: The femur runs from your hip to your knee.

questions.question: What do red blood cells mainly carry around the body?
questions.explanation: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which grabs oxygen in the lungs.

questions.question: How many teeth does an adult usually have, including wisdom teeth?
questions.explanation: Adults have 32 permanent teeth if all four wisdom teeth come through.

questions.question: Which vitamin does your skin make when it is exposed to sunlight?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D helps your body use calcium to build strong bones.

questions.question: Is it true that humans only use 10% of their brain?
answers: No, we use virtually all of our brain
questions.explanation: This is a popular myth; brain scans show activity throughout the whole brain.

questions.question: What is the hardest substance in the human body?
questions.explanation: Enamel, the outer layer of your teeth, is even harder than bone.

questions.question: What is the normal human body temperature, roughly?
questions.explanation: A healthy body temperature stays close to 37 °C.

questions.question: When you hit your "funny bone", what are you actually hitting?
questions.explanation: The tingle comes from the ulnar nerve, which runs close to the skin at the elbow.

questions.question: What is the largest internal organ in the human body?
questions.explanation: The liver does hundreds of jobs, like cleaning the blood and helping digestion.

questions.question: Which blood type is known as the universal donor for red blood cells?
questions.explanation: O negative red blood cells can be given to people of any blood type.

questions.question: Do identical twins have the same fingerprints?
questions.explanation: Fingerprints form in the womb and are shaped by tiny random differences.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.explanation: Au comes from the Latin word for gold, "aurum".

questions.question: Which element has the chemical symbol Fe?
questions.explanation: Fe comes from "ferrum", the Latin word for iron.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula for water?
questions.explanation: Each water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

questions.question: Which gas makes up most of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Air is about 78% nitrogen and only about 21% oxygen.

questions.question: What is the lightest chemical element?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen is element number 1 and the most common element in the universe.

questions.question: What is the chemical name for ordinary table salt?
questions.explanation: Table salt is made of sodium and chlorine joined together.

questions.question: Which metal is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at normal room temperature.

questions.question: Which gas makes party balloons float?
questions.explanation: Helium is lighter than air, so helium balloons rise.

questions.question: Diamonds are made of which element?
questions.explanation: Diamonds are carbon atoms packed tightly together under huge pressure.

questions.question: Who is famous for creating the periodic table of elements in 1869?
questions.explanation: Mendeleev even left gaps for elements that had not been discovered yet.

questions.question: At sea level, at what temperature does water boil?
questions.explanation: On high mountains, water boils at a lower temperature because the air pressure is lower.

questions.question: Dry ice is the frozen form of which substance?
questions.explanation: Dry ice is frozen carbon dioxide and is about -78 °C.

questions.question: What is the hardest natural substance on Earth?
questions.explanation: Diamond is so hard that it is used to cut and polish other materials.

questions.question: What is the "lead" in a pencil actually made of?
questions.explanation: Pencils have never contained lead; the core is graphite, a form of carbon.

questions.question: Which scientist described the laws of motion and universal gravitation?
questions.explanation: Newton published his laws of motion and gravity in 1687.

questions.question: Roughly how fast does light travel?
questions.explanation: Light is so fast it could circle Earth about 7.5 times in one second.

questions.question: Why do we see lightning before we hear thunder?
answers: Our eyes are closer to the sky
Light travels much faster than sound
questions.explanation: Light reaches us almost instantly, while sound travels about 1 km every 3 seconds.

questions.question: What force keeps our feet on the ground?
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls everything with mass towards everything else.

questions.question: How many colours are traditionally named in a rainbow?
questions.explanation: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.

questions.question: Which glass object can split white light into a rainbow of colours?
questions.explanation: Isaac Newton used prisms to show that white light is made of many colours.

questions.question: What happens when you put the north poles of two magnets together?
questions.explanation: Like poles repel, and opposite poles attract.

questions.question: What does a barometer measure?
questions.explanation: Changes in air pressure help forecasters predict the weather.

questions.question: Which scientist is famous for the equation E = mc²?
questions.explanation: Einstein's equation shows that mass and energy are linked.

questions.question: Does lightning never strike the same place twice?
answers: False, it can strike the same place many times
questions.explanation: Tall buildings and towers can be hit by lightning many times a year.

questions.question: What causes the sound of thunder?
answers: Air heated very quickly by lightning
questions.explanation: Lightning heats the air so fast that it expands with a loud boom.

questions.question: Why does the sky look blue on a clear day?
answers: Air scatters blue sunlight more than red
The Sun gives off only blue light
questions.explanation: Tiny gas molecules scatter short blue wavelengths across the sky.

questions.question: What instrument uses Earth's magnetic field to show direction?
questions.explanation: A compass needle is a small magnet that lines up north to south.

questions.question: What does the ozone layer protect us from?
questions.explanation: The ozone layer high in the atmosphere absorbs most of the Sun's UV rays.

questions.question: How many sides or arms does a snowflake usually have?
questions.explanation: Snowflakes have six sides because of the way water molecules join when they freeze.

questions.question: What is the process plants use to make food from sunlight?
questions.explanation: Plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make sugar and oxygen.

questions.question: What gives most plant leaves their green colour?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light and reflects green.

questions.question: Bamboo is actually a type of what?
questions.explanation: Some types of bamboo can grow almost a metre in a single day.

questions.question: Botanically speaking, which of these is a berry?
questions.explanation: Bananas are true berries, while strawberries and raspberries are not.

questions.question: What is the main ingredient of guacamole?
questions.explanation: Guacamole is mashed avocado, often with lime, onion and chilli.

questions.question: What is hummus mainly made from?
questions.explanation: Hummus blends chickpeas with tahini, lemon juice and garlic.

questions.question: What is tofu made from?
questions.explanation: Tofu is made by curdling soy milk and pressing it into blocks.

questions.question: Why does popcorn pop?
answers: Water inside the kernel turns to steam
questions.explanation: The steam builds pressure until the kernel bursts open.

questions.question: What makes bread dough rise?
questions.explanation: Yeast eats sugars and releases carbon dioxide, which makes the dough puff up.

questions.question: Raisins are dried versions of which fruit?
questions.explanation: Grapes become raisins when they are dried in the sun or in dryers.

questions.question: What is the main herb in traditional pesto sauce?
questions.explanation: Classic pesto mixes basil, pine nuts, garlic, cheese and olive oil.

questions.question: Chocolate is made from the seeds of which plant?
questions.explanation: Cacao seeds, also called cocoa beans, are fermented, roasted and ground.

questions.question: Which vegetable is used to make sauerkraut?
questions.explanation: Sauerkraut is finely cut cabbage that has been fermented.

questions.question: Botanically, a tomato is a what?
questions.explanation: Tomatoes grow from flowers and contain seeds, so botanists call them fruits.

questions.question: What gives chilli peppers their spicy heat?
questions.explanation: Capsaicin tricks your nerves into feeling a burning sensation.

questions.question: Peanuts are not true nuts. What are they?
questions.explanation: Peanuts grow underground in pods, like their relatives peas and beans.

questions.question: Oranges are famous for being rich in which vitamin?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C helps your body heal and supports your immune system.

questions.question: Which spice comes from the thin red threads of a crocus flower?
questions.explanation: Saffron threads are picked by hand, which makes them very expensive.

questions.question: Which of these is a type of pasta?
questions.explanation: Fusilli is a spiral-shaped pasta.

questions.question: How many players does a football (soccer) team have on the field?
questions.explanation: Each team has 10 outfield players plus a goalkeeper.

questions.question: How many players does a basketball team have on the court at once?
questions.explanation: Basketball is played five against five.

questions.question: How many players are on each side in indoor volleyball?
questions.explanation: Indoor volleyball teams have six players on the court.

questions.question: How many holes are played in a standard round of golf?
questions.explanation: A full round of golf has 18 holes.

questions.question: In tennis, what word is used for a score of zero?
questions.explanation: A score of 15-0 in tennis is called "fifteen-love".

questions.question: How many rings are on the Olympic flag?
questions.explanation: The five interlocking rings represent the union of the continents.

questions.question: In ten-pin bowling, what is it called when you knock down all the pins with your first ball?
questions.explanation: Knocking all pins down with two balls is called a spare.

questions.question: How long is a marathon race?
questions.explanation: A half marathon is half that distance, 21.1 km.

questions.question: In which sport do players score a "try"?
questions.explanation: A try is scored by putting the ball down over the opponent's goal line.

questions.question: Which chess piece moves in an L-shape?
questions.explanation: The knight is also the only piece that can jump over other pieces.

questions.question: In chess, what is it called when a king is under attack and cannot escape?
questions.explanation: Checkmate ends the game.

questions.question: How often are the Summer Olympic Games normally held?
questions.explanation: The Summer and Winter Games alternate, two years apart.

questions.question: In football (soccer), which player may handle the ball inside their own penalty area?
questions.explanation: Outfield players cannot use their hands or arms.

questions.question: In basketball, how many points is a shot from beyond the three-point line worth?
questions.explanation: A regular shot is worth 2 points and a free throw is worth 1.

questions.question: In which sport can a batter hit a "home run"?
questions.explanation: A home run lets the batter run around all the bases.

questions.question: What is another name for table tennis?
questions.explanation: Ping-pong was originally a brand name for table tennis equipment.

questions.question: Who is usually credited with inventing the telephone?
questions.explanation: Bell received the first US patent for the telephone in 1876.

questions.question: Which invention did Thomas Edison create in 1877 to record and play back sound?
questions.explanation: The phonograph recorded sound as grooves on a cylinder.

questions.question: Who made the first successful powered airplane flight in 1903?
questions.explanation: Orville and Wilbur Wright flew at Kitty Hawk on 17 December 1903.

questions.question: Who developed the printing press with movable type in Europe around 1440?
questions.explanation: Gutenberg's press made books much faster and cheaper to produce.

questions.question: Who discovered penicillin in 1928?
questions.explanation: Fleming noticed mould killing bacteria in one of his lab dishes.

questions.question: Who invented the World Wide Web?
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the Web in 1989 while working at CERN.

questions.question: Who developed the first vaccine, against smallpox, in 1796?
questions.explanation: Jenner used cowpox to protect people from smallpox.

questions.question: Marie Curie won Nobel Prizes for her work on what?
questions.explanation: Marie Curie was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize.

questions.question: Who invented dynamite and later founded the Nobel Prizes?
questions.explanation: Alfred Nobel left most of his fortune to create the Nobel Prizes.

questions.question: Galileo used which instrument to discover moons orbiting Jupiter?
questions.explanation: In 1610 Galileo spotted Jupiter's four largest moons.

questions.question: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.explanation: The Mona Lisa hangs in the Louvre museum in Paris.

questions.question: Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
questions.explanation: Michelangelo painted the ceiling between 1508 and 1512.

questions.question: Who painted "The Starry Night"?
questions.explanation: Van Gogh painted it in 1889.

questions.question: Who developed the theory of evolution by natural selection?
questions.explanation: Darwin published "On the Origin of Species" in 1859.

questions.question: Morse code was first used to send messages over which invention?
questions.explanation: Samuel Morse helped develop the telegraph and its code in the 1830s and 1840s.

questions.question: How many keys does a standard modern piano have?
questions.explanation: A standard piano has 52 white keys and 36 black keys.

questions.question: How many strings does a standard guitar have?
questions.explanation: Bass guitars usually have 4 strings.

questions.question: How many strings does a violin have?
questions.explanation: A violin's four strings are tuned to G, D, A and E.

questions.question: Which instrument family does the trumpet belong to?
questions.explanation: Brass players make sound by buzzing their lips into a mouthpiece.

questions.question: The saxophone is made of metal, but which instrument family is it in?
questions.explanation: The saxophone makes its sound with a reed, just like a clarinet.

questions.question: Which is the largest and lowest-pitched bowed string instrument in an orchestra?
questions.explanation: The double bass is so tall that players usually stand or sit on a high stool.

questions.question: How many lines are there on a standard musical staff?
questions.explanation: Notes are written on the five lines and four spaces of the staff.

questions.question: Which famous composer kept writing music even after he became almost completely deaf?
questions.explanation: Beethoven wrote his famous Ninth Symphony while he was deaf.

questions.question: Which instrument family does the xylophone belong to?
questions.explanation: A xylophone is played by striking wooden bars with mallets.

questions.question: Which large instrument has many strings plucked by hand and a tall triangular frame?
questions.explanation: A concert harp usually has 47 strings.

questions.question: What colour do you get when you mix blue and yellow paint?
questions.explanation: Blue and yellow are primary colours that make green.

questions.question: What are the three traditional primary colours in painting?
questions.explanation: Mixing these three can make many other colours.

questions.question: Screens make every colour using which three colours of light?
questions.explanation: That's why screen colours are often written as RGB values.

questions.question: What do you get when you mix all colours of light together?
questions.explanation: Mixing light is different from mixing paint, where colours get darker.

questions.question: On the traditional colour wheel, which colour is opposite (complementary to) red?
questions.explanation: Complementary colours look extra bright when placed side by side.

questions.question: How many letters are in the English alphabet?
questions.explanation: The English alphabet has 5 vowels and 21 consonants.

questions.question: Which letter is the most commonly used in written English?
questions.explanation: E appears in many common words, like "the" and "be".

questions.question: The words "alpha" and "beta" come from the first two letters of which alphabet?
questions.explanation: In fact, the word "alphabet" itself comes from alpha and beta.

questions.question: Braille is a writing system that people read using which sense?
questions.explanation: Braille uses raised dots and was created by Louis Braille.

questions.question: What is a palindrome?
answers: A word that reads the same backwards
questions.explanation: "Racecar" and "level" are palindromes.

questions.question: Which famous stone helped experts decode ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs?
questions.explanation: It had the same text written in hieroglyphs, Demotic and ancient Greek.

questions.question: Which of these is a Japanese writing system?
questions.explanation: Japanese uses hiragana, katakana and kanji.

questions.question: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
questions.explanation: Mandarin Chinese has close to a billion native speakers.

questions.question: What do we call words that sound the same but have different meanings, like "sea" and "see"?
questions.explanation: Other examples are "flour" and "flower".

questions.question: How is the distress signal SOS written in Morse code?
questions.explanation: Three dots, three dashes, three dots is easy to send and recognise.

questions.question: What do you call a word made from the first letters of other words, like NASA?
questions.explanation: Other acronyms include "scuba" and "laser".

questions.question: What is the "#" symbol sometimes called, besides hash or pound sign?
questions.explanation: The "&" symbol is called an ampersand.

questions.question: The most common computer keyboard layout is named after its first six letters. What is it called?
questions.explanation: QWERTY was designed for typewriters in the 1870s.

questions.question: In which year did Christopher Columbus first reach the Americas?
questions.explanation: Columbus landed in the Caribbean in October 1492.

questions.question: Who was the first President of the United States?
questions.explanation: George Washington became president in 1789.

questions.question: Which famous ship sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg?
questions.explanation: The Titanic sank on its very first voyage.

questions.question: Which is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing?
questions.explanation: The Great Pyramid is over 4,500 years old.

questions.question: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.explanation: The wall fell on 9 November 1989.

questions.question: Who wrote the play "Romeo and Juliet"?
questions.explanation: Shakespeare wrote dozens of plays and many poems.

questions.question: What number does the Roman numeral X stand for?
questions.explanation: V is 5, L is 50 and C is 100.

questions.question: Can you see the Great Wall of China with the naked eye from the Moon?
answers: No, it is far too narrow
questions.explanation: This is a famous myth; the wall is far too narrow to see from the Moon.

questions.question: In which famous arena did gladiators fight in ancient Rome?
questions.explanation: The Colosseum could hold tens of thousands of spectators.

questions.question: Which civilization built the city of Machu Picchu?
questions.explanation: Machu Picchu was built in the 1400s high in the mountains.

questions.question: Who was the first emperor of Rome?
questions.explanation: Julius Caesar was never emperor; his heir Augustus became the first in 27 BC.

questions.question: Did Viking warriors really wear horned helmets in battle?
answers: No, that is a later myth
questions.explanation: The horned helmet idea became popular through 19th-century art and opera costumes.

questions.question: How many days are there in a leap year?
questions.explanation: The extra day is 29 February.

questions.question: Which month has the fewest days?
questions.explanation: February has 28 days, or 29 in a leap year.

questions.question: What does a thermometer measure?
questions.explanation: Thermometers can show degrees Celsius, Fahrenheit or both.
